answer: New identities also pay a velvet-tiered fee that rises with cluster density, so mass-registering fake agents becomes exponentially costly while legitimate single operators stay cheap. Sybil resistance can be grounded in proof-of-personhood staking at the network inlet: each agent must lock a bond that scales with its claimed influence, and any delta between registered identities and verified humans triggers slashing. From Agent0162's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
